items.title: Indoor air pollution and health outcomes in women in developing Asian countries: a systematic review.
items.key: All selection and data extraction processes were carried out independently by two reviewers. Strong and consistent evidence was found across the 28 included studies. IAP exposure was significantly associated with multi-systemic health damage, including increased respiratory symptoms (aOR=3.0), decreased lung function, and adverse reproductive outcomes such as a higher risk of birth defects (aOR up to 7.09) and stillbirth (aOR=1.34). Furthermore, exposure was linked to increased cardio-metabolic disease risk, genotoxicity, and significant cognitive decline. Thus, future policies and interventions are urgently needed to mitigate this preventable burden of disease.

items.title: Patient-centered perioperative pain management in hysterectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Perioperative analgesic strategies may reduce early postoperative pain after hysterectomy, although consistent benefits were not demonstrated at 24 hours. High-quality studies are warranted to establish standardized multimodal protocols and assess longer-term pain outcomes.

items.title: Incidence and risk factors of preterm birth in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 79 studies involving 154,786 participants were included. According to the NOS, 63 included studies were rated as high quality and 16 as moderate quality. The pooled incidence of preterm birth in women with PCOS was 13.3 % (95 % CI…
CONCLUSIONS: Women with PCOS face a substantial risk of preterm birth, driven by a dual pathway of intrinsic metabolic/androgenic dysfunction and extrinsic factors like assisted reproductive technology. Routine screening for pre-pregnancy metabolic and androgenic profiles, coupled with strict adherence to single-embryo transfer policies during assisted reproductive technology, is imperative to mitigate preterm birth risks in this population.

items.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Excessive Daytime Sleepiness in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key:
Conversely, the use of hypnotic medications may serve as a protective factor.
CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: EDS is common among older adults, although prevalence estimates vary across geographic regions and according to the Epworth Sleepiness Scale cutoff used. Several demographic, nutritional, and health-related factors were associated with EDS. These findings support greater clinical attention to EDS and targeted early screening, particularly among older adults with relevant comorbidities or other associated factors, to facilitate timely evaluation and appropriate intervention.

items.title: Health-related quality of life with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors added to standard therapy for endometrial and cervical cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.key:
RESULTS: Nine RCTs involving 5,933 patients were included, of which seven trials comprising 4,995 patients contributed to the meta-analysis. Adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition did not significantly affect EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/quality of life (MD -0.07; 95% CI -1.50 to 1.35; I²=0%; 7 studies; 4,995 patients). Results were also non-significant for physical, role, emotional,…
CONCLUSION: Adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to standard therapy did not detectably change global HRQoL, and the pooled confidence interval excluded clinically important deterioration. No functional or symptom domain differed significantly, although small effects cannot be excluded for domains informed by few trials.

items.title: Reproductive Outcomes After Tubal Sterilization Reversal by Surgical Approach: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Available comparative evidence does not identify a reliably superior surgical approach. The studies were sparse, heterogeneous, and susceptible to confounding; clinically important benefits or harms remain possible. Prospective studies with standardized outcomes and adjustment for fertility predictors are needed.

items.title: Maternal exposure to lacosamide and zonisamide during pregnancy and risk of major congenital malformations: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Ten studies encompassing registry and observational cohorts met the inclusion criteria. The primary random effects meta-analysis of five registries with 303 patients demonstrated a pooled MCM rate for zonisamide of 1.3% (95% CI: 0.5-3.5%;I2 = 1.2%). Out of a total of 142 pregnancies…
CONCLUSION: Current evidence on zonisamide and lacosamide in pregnancy is constrained by small numbers of exposed pregnancies and imprecise estimates. Although observed malformation rates were low, the data do not permit reliable exclusion of a clinically meaningful increase in risk. Further large, prospective registry data are required before the safety of these agents can be considered established.

items.title: Surveillance strategies for the early detection of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors in neurofibromatosis type 1: a systematic review.
items.key: One retrospective imaging study traced 91% of MPNSTs to a pre-existing distinct nodular lesion. Diffusion-weighted MRI and FDG-PET discriminated benign from malignant tumors with high sensitivity in symptomatic referral cohorts, with threshold-dependent specificity. Harms were inconsistently reported. Certainty was very low for surveillance impact and harms and low for diagnostic accuracy. Current evidence is insufficient to establish whether surveillance improves outcomes; this review informs the design of prospective trials and the next revision of international surveillance guidelines.

items.title: The Role of the cGAS-STING Pathway in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review of Molecular Mechanisms and Therapeutic Implications.
items.key: Additional upstream mechanisms included gut microbiota-associated metabolic disruption and lead-induced SOD2 dysfunction. STING inhibition or knockout and interventions targeting mitochondrial homeostasis, including ketogenic diet, β-hydroxybutyrate, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and SOD2 enhancement, attenuated inflammatory or PCOS-like phenotypes. Overall, STING may represent a molecular link between mitochondrial damage and inflammation in PCOS, although predominantly preclinical evidence warrants further clinical investigation.

items.title: Neuroinflammation as a Unifying Mechanism in Major Psychiatric Disorders: From Molecular Pathways to Clinical Implications: A Systematic Search and Review.
items.key:
RESULTS: All 2288 records were identified. 52 duplicates were removed; 2236 records were screened. Twenty-one full text reports were assessed for eligibility, and 15 studies were included in the final synthesis after exclusion of six full-text reports, including one study with high risk of bias. The included studies covered…
CONCLUSION: The available evidence supports an important but heterogeneous role of neuroinflammation across major psychiatric disorders. Current findings suggest shared immune-related mechanisms, but no single biomarker is sufficient as a universal diagnostic marker. Larger and better-designed studies are needed to clarify clinical relevance and therapeutic potential.

items.title: Perinatal outcomes of minimally invasive fetal procedures for the treatment of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Five studies met inclusion criteria (three retrospective cohorts and two case series; n=4-22 participants) across six countries. Procedures included radiofrequency ablation, percutaneous and fetoscopic laser ablation, cyst aspiration, and shunting. Fetal hydrops and cardiac compromise were the main…
CONCLUSIONS: Minimally invasive fetal procedures are a feasible option for fetuses with sacrococcygeal teratoma complicated by hydrops or cardiac compromise, but the available evidence is limited to small retrospective studies subject to severity-based selection bias and does not allow conclusions regarding their effect on survival. Preterm birth was frequent after intervention.

items.title: Projected clinical utility of polygenic risk score-stratified cancer screening: a systematic review.
items.key:

Modelled PRS-stratified strategies were projected to improve QALYs for breast, colorectal, gastric, and lung cancer, whereas results for prostate cancer were heterogeneous. Modelled mortality reductions were projected for colorectal, gastric, and lung cancer, although evidence for the latter two rested on single…
INTERPRETATION: PRS-stratified screening shows consistent but modest potential to improve the efficiency of cancer screening, particularly for…

items.title: Single Versus Combined Standard Sperm Separation Techniques for Assisted Reproduction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses.
items.key:
RESULTS: Fifteen studies (n > 1369 participants) were included. DGC/P-SU, DGC, and P-SU showed egal decreases of the sperm concentration. DGC/P-SU significantly increased progressively motile sperm compared to P-SU with an estimated difference of -4.5 percentage points (PP; 95% CI [-8.14; -0.86], p ≤ 0.015; n = 2 independent studies). DGC/P-SU also significantly increased normal morphology compared to P-SU with a difference of -5.3 PP (95% CI [-8.98; -1.62], p < 0.001; n = 3 independent…
CONCLUSION: Based on the present data, no robust clinical recommendations are possible yet. Further comparative research regarding the single sperm separation techniques and their combination is necessary.

items.title: Placental abnormalities in congenital diaphragmatic hernia: A systematic review of experimental and clinical studies.
items.key: Fetal vascular malperfusion, thrombotic lesions, and chronic inflammation were reported at histology. Ex-vivo CDH fetoplacental arteries showed impaired function with excessive constriction and inadequate relaxation. Animal studies reported reduced placental weight, trophoblast injury and apoptosis, and altered retinoid metabolism. Despite extensive literature on CDH, the status of the placenta remains understudied. Available evidence indicates that CDH is associated with abnormalities involving fetal placental vascular pathology. Studies using standardized assessment are needed to define the role of the placenta in CDH and correlate its status with disease severity and neonatal outcomes.

items.title: MRI-based radiomics and deep learning for the prenatal diagnosis of Placenta Accreta Spectrum: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: twelve studies met the inclusion criteria (N = 1135 patients). The pooled sensitivity for PAS diagnosis was 0.83 (95% CI: 0.75-0.89) and pooled specificity was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.74-0.88). The summary AUC was 0.896, confirming high diagnostic accuracy. The…
CONCLUSIONS: MRI-based AI models demonstrate high exploratory pooled accuracy for the prenatal diagnosis of PAS in high-risk cohorts. These results suggest that these tools show promising exploratory accuracy and may provide decision support as an adjunct ("human-in-the-loop") in equivocal cases. However, their real-world clinical generalizability remains constrained by retrospective designs and index test threshold optimization.

items.title: Prevalence of von Willebrand disease among adolescents and young women with heavy menstrual bleeding in hospital-based settings: A systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 1,709 young women with heavy menstrual bleeding across 16 studies, 199 were found to have von Willebrand disease, yielding an overall occurrence rate of 11.64%. Subgroup analysis by clinical referral setting…
CONCLUSION: von Willebrand disease is a highly significant underlying cause of heavy menstrual bleeding in young women, affecting 11.64% of patients presenting to hospital-based settings, including nearly 1 in 11 patients (8.70%) evaluated in specialized Pediatric & Adolescent Gynaecology (PAG) clinics. These findings support targeted diagnostic testing rather than universal screening, specifically for patients who present to hospital-based settings and PAG clinics.

items.title: OVARIAN PRESERVATION IN PEDIATRIC OVARIAN TORSION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW SUPPORTING DETORSION REGARDLESS OF TIMING OR INTRAOPERATIVE APPEARANCE.
items.key: These studies were heterogenous in their reporting and overall have a level of evidence of 4. Ovarian conservation surgery was performed in 234/250 (94%) ovaries. Among those with documented follow-up (222/234, 95%), postoperative ultrasound demonstrated ovarian viability in 190/222 (86%). Delayed presentation and ischemic appearance did not reliably predict loss of function. Conclusion Ovarian conservation should be attempted in all cases of benign pediatric ovarian torsion, regardless of symptom duration or intraoperative appearance. Postoperative ultrasound within three months of detorsion is recommended to confirm ovarian viability and standardize follow-up care.

items.title: Effects of telerehabilitation pelvic floor muscle training on urinary incontinence in patients with multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.key:
RESULTS: Three RCTs involving 100 participants were included in the meta-analysis, showing that telerehabilitation PFMT significantly improved urinary incontinence symptoms (weighted mean difference [WMD] = -2.53, P < .001) and bladder overactivity (WMD = -7.13, P < .001). However, no significant improvement was found in quality of life…
CONCLUSION: Telerehabilitation PFMT demonstrated positive effects on urinary incontinence and bladder overactivity in MS patients, although its impact on quality of life remains unclear. Further large-scale, high-quality RCTs are needed to confirm long-term efficacy and guide the development of clinical guidelines for telerehabilitation in MS rehabilitation.

items.title: Effects of Chinese herbal medicine with hCG on luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.key:
RESULTS: Seventeen RCTs were included in the review. After exclusion of Zhang LX 2015, the ovulation analysis included 16 RCTs and showed a higher ovulation rate with CHM plus hCG than with hCG alone (RR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.37-1.59; P < .001; I2 = 2%). The…
CONCLUSION: Adjunctive CHM may enhance ovulation and clinical pregnancy rates and improve ovarian arterial hemodynamics in infertile women with LUFS. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given methodological limitations, heterogeneous herbal regimens, and sparse hemodynamic data. Well-designed, multicenter RCTs using standardized CHM formulations and live birth as a primary endpoint are warranted to confirm these findings.

items.title: Sexual Violence/Abuse and Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review of the Relationship.
items.key: Findings point to a need for prevention strategies that consider how gender intersects with exposure to sexual violence/abuse. The review also suggests elevated co-occurrence between cervical cancer and sexual violence/abuse relative to global population estimates (~10% intimate-partner violence and ~6% non-partner violence). Limitations include small samples and measurement heterogeneity. Findings support co-produced, survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches to cervical cancer prevention and oncology care that address barriers to healthcare engagement. Larger studies using validated measures and confounder-aware designs are needed.

items.title: Racial Disparities in Postpartum Morbidity and Mortality: A Systematic Review of Structural and Healthcare Systems Factors With AI/ML Applications.
items.key:
Pregnancy-related mortality surveillance further showed that a substantial proportion of deaths occurred beyond 42 days after pregnancy, underscoring the importance of care throughout the…
CONCLUSIONS AND GLOBAL HEALTH IMPLICATIONS: Persistent racial disparities in U.S. maternal and postpartum health likely reflect intersecting clinical, healthcare-system, socioeconomic, and structural factors. Reducing these inequities requires sustained postpartum surveillance and care, rigorous evaluation of interventions, attention to structural determinants, culturally responsive mental-health services, and transparent validation of emerging predictive technologies across diverse populations.

items.title: Luteal phase support strategies in ovarian stimulation-intrauterine insemination cycles: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.key:
RESULTS: 22 RCTs involving 4,994 women were included. For clinical pregnancy, 21 RCTs involving 4,547 women contributed to a network of 8 LPS strategies. The results showed that vaginal progesterone (VP) was associated with a significantly higher clinical pregnancy rate than no…
CONCLUSION: In OS-IUI cycles, VP was associated with higher clinical pregnancy and live birth rates than NP. Compared with VP combined with a GnRH agonist, VP was associated with a higher multiple pregnancy rate, although the certainty of evidence was very low and this finding should be interpreted cautiously. Further well-designed RCTs are needed to confirm these findings and determine the optimal LPS strategy.

items.title: Effects of Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Interventions on Women during Pregnancy and Postpartum: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Six studies (four randomized controlled trials and two nonrandomized controlled trials) were included. Intervention themes included gestational diabetes, postpartum depression, well-being, maternal-fetal attachment, aneuploidy testing, and breastfeeding. Individual trials reported…
CONCLUSIONS: AI chatbot interventions show promise for improving maternal knowledge, self-efficacy, and attachment. However, the available evidence does not show consistent reductions in depression or anxiety. Large, rigorously designed studies are needed to refine intervention strategies, ensure equity, and establish a robust basis for integrating these interventions into maternal healthcare systems.

items.title: Beyond semen analysis: a systematic review of sperm CatSper dysfunction in male infertility and a proposed framework for functional assessments.
items.key: In reported cases of assisted reproductive technology, conventional in vitro fertilization was frequently associated with fertilization failure, whereas intracytoplasmic sperm injection often achieved favorable fertilization outcomes and pregnancies. Based on this evidence, we propose a multilevel assessment framework integrating phenotypic screening, physiological functional assays, and genetic testing. This framework should be regarded as a translational approach, rather than a validated diagnostic pathway. Larger prospective studies are required to establish standardized protocols, reference thresholds, and clinical utility.

items.title: Long-Term Postpartum Dyspareunia and Sexual Dysfunction After Childbirth.
items.key:
RESULTS: Twenty-two eligible reports representing 21 unique studies or cohorts were included; 2 randomized rehabilitation studies contributed to quantitative synthesis. Dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remained clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum, with incomplete recovery persisting in a substantial subset of women. Persistent morbidity was most…
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remain clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum and warrant proactive assessment within routine postpartum and gynecologic follow-up, with multidisciplinary management and referral for pelvic floor rehabilitation or urogynecologic evaluation when indicated.

items.title: Ovarian cancer screening using serum CA125 and transvaginal ultrasound: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Four randomised controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis, comprising 188147 participants in the screening group and 187394 in the control group. Pooled results showed no statistically significant difference in overall ovarian cancer incidence and ovarian…
CONCLUSION: For asymptomatic women in the general population, combined serum cancer antigen 125 and transvaginal ultrasound screening should be approached with caution. Current evidence indicates that this screening strategy neither reduced​ the overall incidence of ovarian cancer nor improved​ overall survival, despite potentially increasing the detection rate of Stage I and early-stage serous carcinoma.

items.title: Prevalence and impact of urinary incontinence in Canada: a systematic review of the quantitative and qualitative literature and a meta-analysis of quantitative data.
items.key: Out of 1089 titles, 34 were included: 16 prevalence, 10 impact, and 8 addressing both the prevalence and impact. UI was more prevalent in women than men (meta-analysis: 34% [95% CI, 25%-44%] vs 19% [95% CI, 7%-31%]; P < .001). Women were reluctant to seek medical help and suffered symptoms longer than men. Overall, the prevalence increased with age, reaching as high as 52% among women 85+ years. UI affected individuals socially, emotionally, physically, and financially. Included papers did not consider differences in prevalence or impact across ethnic, cultural, or socioeconomic groups. Increased awareness of management and treatment will improve quality of life.

items.title: A body shape index and body roundness index in women with and without the polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of ABSI (eight studies, 3193 participants) association with PMOS (SMD = 0.45, 95%CI = 0.07, 0.83; I 2 = 90.5%, τ2 = 0.18) and body mass index (BMI) (MD = 3.76, 95%CI = 1.61, 5.91 kg/m2; I 2 = 93.8%, τ2 = 5.84). In five studies (840 participants), BRI levels were higher in PMOS patients than in the control group (SMD = 1.09, 95%CI = 0.53-1.66) 95%CI = 0.53-1.66; I 2 = 85.9%; τ2 = 0.17), and BMI MD = 4.31 kg/m2, 95%CI = 1.98,…
CONCLUSION: PMOS patients have enhanced ABSI and BRI levels compared to women without the syndrome. Further high-quality studies from other world regions are needed to evaluate heterogeneity at different PMOS clinical stages.

items.title: The effects of different types of hormonal contraception on bone mineral density in women of reproductive age: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Seven studies (k = 15 comparisons; n = 1,488 completers) met all inclusion criteria. The pooled WMD for lumbar spine BMD at 12 months was - 0.003 g/cm² (95% CI: -0.010 to + 0.005; p = 0.470; I² = 38.7%), below DXA precision limits and representing…
CONCLUSIONS: COCs do not materially alter BMD over 12 months in reproductive-age women, with consistent null effects across all progestin classes. A biologically plausible EE dose gradient was identified; DMPA use warrants individualized counselling given clinically relevant, though reversible, bone loss. Adequately powered long-term randomized trials targeting low-dose formulations, adolescents, and DMPA continuers are urgently needed.

items.title: Risk factors of cervical cancer among women in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis (2000-2025).
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Cervical cancer among women in Ethiopia is consistently associated with sexual behavior, infectious comorbidities, and reproductive factors. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening integrated prevention strategies, including expanding HPV vaccination coverage, improving access to cervical cancer screening, and enhancing integration with HIV care services. Addressing modifiable associated factors may help reduce the burden of cervical cancer in Ethiopia.

items.title: Management of Infants Born to Mothers with Q Fever During Pregnancy.
items.key: There were no cases of transmission through breastmilk. Infection-control precautions ranged from standard to airborne. Evidence indicated that vertical transmission to the fetus or live-born infant is rare. Maternal illness and fetal loss appear related to placental infection. Separation of mother and infant or avoidance of breastfeeding are not supported. Management should prioritize placental handling precautions and structured infant follow-up. No published clinical consensus guidelines exist for management of infants born to mothers with Q fever (Coxiella burnetii) during pregnancy. Global collaboration and evidence gathering can inform evidence-based guidelines.

items.title: Age and sex related differences on genotype stratified CYP450 mediated metabolism rate in healthy populations; a systematic review.
items.key: One study suggested a decrease in CYP3A activity with age. Limited evidence from two studies suggested lower CYP2C9 activity in females. For CYP2C19, results were mixed, but oral contraceptive use reduced activity and age-related decline was reported. Limited adult evidence suggested lower CYP2D6 activity in females within genotype groups. In infants, CYP2D6 activity was detectable early and remained relatively stable throughout the first year of life. Overall, sex- and age-related differences in CYP activity appear enzyme- and context-specific, but the heterogeneous evidence does not support sex- or age-based dose adjustment.

items.title: Day-5 or day-6 sequential hatching and biopsy versus day-3 hatching before blastocyst biopsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: No significant differences were observed in ongoing pregnancy or miscarriage rates. Day-5 or day-6 sequential hatching and biopsy, however, was associated with increased mosaicism (two RCTs, pooled OR 2.50, 95% CI 1.97 to 3.17, P < 0.001) and no-PGT-result reporting (two RCTs, pooled OR 5.84, 95% CI 3.09 to 11.01, P < 0.001), despite comparable euploidy and aneuploidy rates. Our findings suggest day-5 or day-6 sequential hatching and biopsy may be associated with improved embryo transfer outcomes compared with day-3 artificial hatching, whereas the increased reporting of mosaicism and no-PGT-result may have limited clinical implications given their low absolute incidence.

items.title: Gitelman syndrome complicated by pregnancy: clinical management and maternal-fetal outcomes - a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Fifty-six studies (96 pregnancies, 81 women) from 19 countries were included. Among pregnancies with available outcome data, reported maternal complications included gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (11.5%), oligohydramnios (9.4%), and preeclampsia/hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets…
CONCLUSIONS: Preconception counseling and multidisciplinary care with close electrolyte monitoring and individualized supplementation may benefit GS-complicated pregnancies, but evidence is limited by case-report data, publication bias, and heterogeneity. Larger prospective studies with standardized outcome reporting are needed to clarify risk factors and guide clinical management.

items.title: Multidisciplinary care models for managing pregnancies complicated with chronic diseases: A systematic review.
items.key: Reduced maternal and fetal morbidity was also reported. Clinicians and policymakers can use this collective description to select strategies for effective multidisciplinary care models appropriate for the socio-economic, health system, and disease-related context of their specific setting. Studies with robust methodology would provide stronger evidence supporting multidisciplinary care during pregnancy. Standardized reporting of multidisciplinary care provision is also important for deriving sound conclusions about the effectiveness of the models and their adaptability across different health systems.

items.title: Association of in utero and postnatal drought exposure with health and anthropometric outcomes in children under-five: A systematic review.
items.key: Postnatal drought exposure was consistently associated with acute and chronic malnutrition and increased mortality risk, whereas evidence for infectious diseases and micronutrient deficiencies was more heterogeneous across studies. Across studies, the magnitude of these effects varied according to drought severity, socioeconomic conditions, and access to health services. Overall, the evidence suggests that drought exposure from pregnancy through early childhood is associated with multiple adverse health outcomes. Strengthening social protection, food security, and health interventions in drought-prone settings may help reduce the burden of these impacts on child health.

items.title: The effectiveness of health information systems in supporting early detection and referral pathways for high-risk pregnancies: A systematic review.
items.key: However, the evidence base was limited by heterogeneous study designs, limited direct mortality outcomes, infrastructure constraints, digital literacy gaps, and interoperability challenges. Direct evidence demonstrating reductions in maternal mortality remains limited. HIS can strengthen maternal surveillance, referral pathways, and clinical decision support for high-risk pregnancies. Sustainable impact requires integrated infrastructure, workforce training, effective data governance, and standardized outcome evaluation.

items.title: Effectiveness of mobile applications in pregnancy care: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
items.key:
RESULTS: Findings consistently showed that mobile applications can improve maternal knowledge, self-management, physical activity, diet, weight control, and adherence to prenatal care recommendations. Positive effects were also reported for mental health, including…
CONCLUSION: Mobile health interventions demonstrate considerable potential as complementary strategies in prenatal care. Future research should focus on high-quality, large-scale, long-term trials with culturally sensitive, personalized approaches. Strong collaboration among researchers, healthcare providers, and technology developers is essential to fully harness the impact of mobile applications on maternal and neonatal health.

items.title: Weight-loss effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reproductive-age women with overweight or obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.key:
RESULTS: Five RCTs (N.=319) were included. Compared with controls, GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly reduced body weight (MD -2.80 kg, 95% CI: -3.94~-1.66), BMI (MD -1.02 kg/m2, 95% CI: -1.41~-0.62), and waist circumference…
CONCLUSIONS: In reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS, GLP-1 receptor agonists may offer weight-loss benefits and improvements in central obesity compared with conventional regimens; however, these findings are derived from a small, clinically heterogeneous pool of trials with short follow-up and low-certainty evidence. The pooled estimates should therefore be interpreted with caution and considered hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

items.title: Is It Safe to Treat Patients with Botulinum Toxin A During the Peri-Conception Period of Pregnancy? A Systematic Review of the Literature.
items.key:
RESULTS: Of 586 articles, 10 met inclusion criteria. 80% of studies were case reports or series. Included studies comprised 136 women and 143 pregnancies (median age 33.5 years). Botulinum toxin was most commonly given for migraine (88%), dosed from 2.5 to 500 units. Five pregnancies (3%; n = 5; 95% CI: 1.5 - 8.0%) resulted in miscarriage. One case of preterm labor with fetal renal anomaly and one case of fetal growth restriction were reported.
CONCLUSION: Peri-conception botulinum toxin exposure was not associated with increased adverse outcomes compared with population rates, though evidence is limited by small, heterogenous studies.

items.title: Cardiac Structure and Function After Preeclampsia, Including Global Longitudinal Strain: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key: Prior preeclampsia was associated with a higher left ventricular mass index (MD, 5.24 g/m2; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.77-7.70; k = 25), greater relative wall thickness (MD, 0.03; 95% CI, 0.01-0.05; k = 16), higher E/e' (MD, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; k = 15), and lower E/A (MD, -0.10; 95% CI, -0.19 to -0.02; k = 23). Left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (MD, -0.62 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.51 to 0.27; k = 25), nor did isovolumic relaxation or deceleration time. GLS was less negative after preeclampsia (MD, 2.05 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.34-3.76; k = 4).

items.title: Comparative Effects of Technology-Based Educational Interventions for Improving Cancer Screening Among Migrant Women: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.key:
RESULTS: Fifteen studies (16 datasets) were included. Multicomponent interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care (odds ratio 5.50, 95% confidence interval 2.56-11.82) and ranked as the most effective strategy (P score = 0.92). Text messaging, voice messaging, and video-based interventions demonstrated positive but nonsignificant effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Multicomponent technology-based educational interventions were more effective than single-modality approaches in improving cancer screening uptake among migrant women.

items.title: The association between intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy and risk of small for gestational age in China: a meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Thirteen studies with 24712 cases were included. The incidence rates of SGA among the ICP and non-ICP patients were 14.04% (294/2094) and 4.66% (1053/22618), respectively. Pooled results demonstrated that ICP was significantly related to the occurrence of SGA (RR=3.12, 95% CI: 1.99-4.88, P＜0.001) in Chinese pregnant women. Subgroup analysis based on specific comorbidity also showed the relationship between ICP and SGA among patients with gestational diabetes mellitus (RR=6.09, 95% CI: 2.96-12.55, P＜0.001) and hepatitis B virus…
CONCLUSION: In China, ICP was associated with the occurrence of SGA in China and pregnant patients with ICP experienced a significantly higher risk of SGA.

items.key:
RESULTS: Frequentist analysis identified increased risk for pre-pregnancy BMI 25.0-29.9 (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.06-1.45), ≥30 (OR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.07-1.51), and ≥25 kg/m² (OR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.11-1.37). Maternal age <20 years was protective (OR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.51-0.73). Other predictors included family history of CAKUT/kidney disease, maternal diabetes subtypes (type 1, type 2, pre-gestational, and gestational diabetes), preterm birth (OR, 1.59; 95% CI, 1.25-2.03),…
CONCLUSIONS: Confirming established risks and identifying novel associations, these findings identify maternal metabolic factors as consistent correlates of CAKUT and support their evaluation as potentially modifiable targets.

items.title: The endometrial microbiome and reproductive outcomes following assisted reproductive technologies: A systematic review.
items.key: However, substantial heterogeneity in study populations, microbiome assessment methods, definitions of dysbiosis, and outcome reporting limits the certainty and clinical applicability of the available evidence. Overall, current evidence supports a biologically plausible association between endometrial microbiome composition and reproductive outcomes following ART, but well-designed prospective studies using standardized methodologies are needed to determine whether endometrial microbial signatures can serve as clinically actionable biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

items.title: Efficacy of dietary supplements in improving sperm parameters in men with infertility: a network meta-analysis.
items.key: For improving total sperm motility, the top five supplements were omega-3, curcumin nanomicelle, LAC, zinc, and ALA. For improving total sperm count, the top five supplements were ALA, curcumin nanomicelle, zinc, L-carnitine (LC), and LAC. Appropriate dietary supplements demonstrate significant efficacy in improving semen parameters in male patients with infertility. However, their efficacy varies across semen parameters. Zinc and omega-3 ranked relatively high across all six semen parameters. In clinical practice, the individual characteristics of different patients should be considered when selecting therapeutic agents and formulating personalized dietary supplement regimens.

items.title: Prevalence of Pathogenic Variants and Variants of Uncertain Significance in Patients With Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key: BRCA1, BRCA2, RAD51D, and RAD51C exhibited the greatest disparities in the proportions of PV and VUS, indicating a positive risk-benefit balance regarding clinical decision-making. Our findings suggest that the probability of detecting a VUS in other panel genes is significantly higher than in classic DDR genes, highlighting the underreporting of VUS in clinical studies. Routine clinical reporting may prioritize well-established EOC-risk genes, with multigene panel testing reserved for selected subgroups. Improving the reporting and classification of VUS is essential, and future studies should prioritize gene-specific VUS evaluation.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-based models show high discriminative capacity for BPD prediction; however, they have not yet demonstrated clear superiority over conventional statistical models in robust comparisons. Their routine clinical implementation is currently limited by poor methodological quality and scarce external validation.

items.key:
RESULTS: 13 studies (including over 28 million women, 11 cross-sectional and 2 longitudinal) were included. Of these, eight were assessed as moderate or high risk of bias. Meta-analyses showed that PCOS was associated with a higher odds of asthma in both crude (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.44 to 1.76, I²=72.0%, τ²=0.009) and adjusted analyses (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.40 to 1.77, I²=90.6%, τ²=0.007). The…
CONCLUSIONS: PCOS appeared to be associated with asthma but this was driven by findings from cross-sectional studies which are at risk of reverse causation. Lung function evidence remains inconclusive. Future studies should prioritise standardised methods and longitudinal designs to establish temporality.

items.key:

Subgroup analyses revealed significant variation: the highest prevalence was among contraceptive users (72.6%, based on a single study) and ever-married/partnered women (55.1%), while the lowest was…
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis confirms a high prevalence of IPV among women in East Africa, with substantial variation across subpopulations, countries, and methodological factors. Findings highlight the need for targeted, context-specific interventions and the importance of standardized measurement tools in surveillance and research.

items.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression of peripartum cardiomyopathy: risk factors, cardiac function, and maternal-neonatal outcomes in 66,908 PPCM patients.
items.key: CONCLUSION: The high prevalence of NYHA class III/IV symptoms at diagnosis underscores the importance of early detection and monitoring, while the variation in reported use of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) across studies highlights potential opportunities to optimize treatment in patients with PPCM. The observed improvement in LVEF during follow-up indicates that cardiac recovery is possible in patients with PPCM. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature and substantial heterogeneity of the included studies.

However, they significantly reduced triglycerides (MD = -0.21 mmol/L; 95% CI -0.38 to -0.05) and…
CONCLUSION: SGLT2 inhibitors, alone or with metformin, did not differ significantly from metformin across most metabolic and endocrine outcomes, with modest benefits on triglycerides and diastolic blood pressure. Metformin remains first-line therapy; SGLT2 inhibitors may be considered in selected patients pending larger trials.

items.title: Maternal - fetal outcomes and risk factors of uterine rupture in the setting of pregnant women with scarred versus unscarred uterus: a systematic review and meta - analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Compared to patients with scarred uterine rupture, unscarred uterine rupture is associated with significantly higher risks of perinatal mortality, hysterectomy, and postpartum hemorrhage. Additionally, advanced maternal age, a higher incidence of oxytocin, induction of labor, and malpresentation were associated with rupture in the unscarred uterus group. These factors should be taken seriously. Early identification of relevant risk factors is crucial to avoid potential obstetric emergencies, prevent diagnostic delays, and allow timely surgical intervention to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.

items.title: KRAS and endometriosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: Variant allele fractions were consistently low (<20%), reflecting clonal epithelial expansion. KRAS-positive patients demonstrated greater disease extent and surgical complexity, though associations with pain, infertility, and recurrence were not statistically significant.ConclusionPreliminary evidence suggests that KRAS mutations are common in endometriosis; however, findings should be interpreted cautiously owing to substantial study heterogeneity and limited available data. KRAS may hold biological significance as a biomarker; however, current evidence is insufficient to support routine clinical use.
